movie.title: I Am Frankelda
movie.overview: A gifted young writer in 19th-century Mexico journeys into her subconscious and comes face to face with characters from her own spooky stories.

reviews.author: Chris Sawin
reviews.content:
I Am Frankelda is Mexico’s first stop-motion animated feature film. Written, directed, and produced by Rodolfo and Arturo Ambriz, the Ambriz brothers are proteges of Guillermo del Toro and even dedicate the film to the Mexican filmmaker. The film is a Mexican production produced by Cartoon Network Latin America and Warner Bros. Discovery. 

The Ambriz brothers did a miniseries consisting of five 12-minute episodes entitled Frankelda’s Book of Spooks, which I Am Frankelda is essentially an expansion of. The series looks like it features the same characters and cinematic realms that I Am Frankelda showcases, but is more focused on the stories Frankelda has written in her book. I Am Frankelda is the origin of both Francisca Imelda in the 1870s and a disintegrating nightmare realm where she is drawn to an owl boy named Herneval. Since Frankelda’s Book of Spooks can currently be found on HBO Max, it seems like I Am Frankelda will eventually be available there. 

Francis’s imagination was troublesome for her as a child. She has always been writing, but her vivid imagination always resulted in her grandmother scolding her and encouraging her to do more feminine activities. The two realms were bridged from the beginning, with Francis’ writing being the common connection. She dreamed about the nightmare realm from a young age and wrote about it. 

Herneval is a prince whose royal family rules over the nightmare realm. His father and mother, the king and queen, are kind and compassionate, while their empathy for others is often seen as a weakness. Their realm is falling apart because there hasn’t been a decent nightmare in years. 

A giant green spider named Procustes is the royal nightmarer. He is in charge of writing horrific nightmares that would allow their realm to flourish. But Procustes hasn’t written anything in years. His time is spent trying to keep his job with mind games. Since he has had the royal nightmarer title for so long, he believes his writing ability is greater than it truly is. 

Years pass, and Herneval and Francis are now adults. Francis attempts to get published, but her horror and fantasy stories are seen as too fanciful. She is encouraged to write in a more realistic genre, like romance, and she takes it personally. She adopts the Frankelda moniker as a new pen name to continue writing as the best fantasy and horror author ever.

Herneval’s parents are now dying, and the nightmare realm is on the verge of deteriorating completely. Herneval has been following and reading Francis’ stories all this time – traveling to her realm despite it being forbidden. He wants her to be the new royal nightmarer to save his realm and his parents. Procustes becomes jealous and intends to have Frankelda write for him for eternity. 

I Am Frankelda takes a lot of inspiration from the likes of The Nightmare Before Christmas and The Neverending Story. The importance of writing and fiction is crucial to the storytelling of the film. Francis’ stories fail to make an impact in her realm, but are like a series of undiscovered gold mines in the nightmare realm. 

It’s also bizarre that the writing of the film is so elongated. I Am Frankelda is nearly two hours long, which feels like an eternity for an animated film. The film is so dialogue-heavy, as well. With so many exceptional monsters and unique creatures in the film, it feels criminal that they spend more time talking than they do being scary or menacing. 

The ending isn’t entirely satisfying either. I Am Frankelda leaves the story up in the air with a ton of unanswered plot points and major developments. It ends on a serious cliffhanger that impacts both realms simultaneously. It’s a bold move considering in this day and age, especially on a fickle streaming giant like HBO Max, that cancels fully completed Warner Bros. Films whenever the wind blows the wrong way, hinting at a sequel that may or may not come to fruition. 

For the most part, I Am Frankelda is beautiful to look at. The puppets used in the animated film are brimming with intricate details, and the film itself gushes with vibrant colors and superb lighting. In a lot of old cartoons, you can typically tell what item someone is going to interact with because it either has more detail or it's a different color. The mouths in I Am Frankelda are consistently different colors, which is a bit distracting. Many of the typical bean-shaped mouths are also flat and give off South Park or Robot Chicken vibes. 

The backgrounds are littered with the same amount of detail. The nightmare realm is surrounded by a cloud-infested sea with waving white arms and hands. Structures are made up of various colored eyeballs, talons, and wings buried inside massive tree trunks and branches. When a nightmare is written, the royal family places it on a podium next to a tree with cobwebs inside. The cobwebs are then used as a harp to play the freshly written nightmares. 

There are incredible, spooky elements throughout I Am Frankelda. A crocodile fishing in the cloud sea is seen moments later with its flesh dissolving from its bones. The nightmare realm features nasty perfection like a two-headed griffin, a mammoth skeleton, and a blindfolded magic coyote. The film is a visual feast for animation fans. 

A story worth telling is told in a roundabout way that would benefit from being much more concise. I Am Frankelda needed an editor or a ghost writer to tighten things up. The film feels like it’s about 15-20 minutes too long. Overall, I Am Frankelda is an animated triumph that is a bit rough around the edges.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: In 19th-century Mexico, a gifted young writer enters her own subconscious to confront the haunting creatures and characters born from her terrifying stories.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Set against the backdrop of 19th-century Mexico, *I Am Frankelda* follows a talented young author who finds herself drawn into the eerie depth of her own mind. As she navigates a surreal realm filled with spooky monsters and dark manifestations of her imagination, she must face the very characters she brought to life. Along the way, she discovers the emotional weight and power hidden within her creative voice. Ultimately, her journey becomes a fight not only to survive her darkest tales, but to embrace her identity as a storyteller.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: In the heart of 19th-century Mexico, Frankelda is a passionate young writer whose vivid imagination crafts terrifying yet captivating stories. Feeling misunderstood by the world around her, she seeks solace in her craft, unaware of the thin boundary separating her inner world from reality. One day, Frankelda is unexpectedly pulled into a mysterious and haunting subconscious landscape populated by the grotesque monsters and tragic figures of her own creation. As she ventures deeper into this dark fantasy realm, she must navigate treacherous environments while uncovering the underlying emotional truths behind each character she wrote. Guided by her wit and growing courage, she encounters both hostile entities and unexpected allies within her mind. Each encounter forces her to confront her deepest fears, doubts, and bottled-up artistic struggles that fueled her tales. As the line between creator and creation blurs, Frankelda realizes that defeating her nightmare visions requires understanding and accepting them. Through sheer resilience and belief in her artistic expression, she works to reclaim control over her narratives and her psyche. Ultimately, Frankelda triumphs over her inner shadows, returning to her world with a renewed sense of purpose and confidence in her unique voice.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Set in 19th-century Mexico, *I Am Frankelda* is an enchanting animated dark fantasy that delves into the delicate power of storytelling and self-discovery. The narrative revolves around a brilliantly creative young writer named Frankelda, whose macabre imagination sets her apart from society. When she finds herself transported directly into her own subconscious mind, she is forced to confront a haunting world populated by the monsters, spirits, and tragic figures of her own stories. Rich in atmospheric horror, family-friendly adventure, and emotional drama, this gothic journey explores how the tales we create reflect our deepest fears and hidden strengths. Without giving away its twists, the story serves as an inspiring and spine-tingling testament to embracing one's imagination, finding one's true voice, and making peace with the shadows within.

story_structure.climax: Frankelda faces the ultimate manifestation of her deepest fears and creative anxieties in a decisive confrontation that tests her resolve and self-identity.
story_structure.conflict: Frankelda's imaginative creations cross over from the page into her reality, trapping her in a mysterious realm where her own stories come to life.
story_structure.resolution: By accepting every part of her mind—both dark and light—Frankelda reclaims her narrative voice, emerging as a empowered storyteller who commands her own destiny.
story_structure.introduction: In 19th-century Mexico, Frankelda, a passionate young writer with a dark and vivid imagination, crafts eerie tales while navigating personal turmoil and societal constraints.
story_structure.risingAction: Journeying deeper into her mind, Frankelda encounters a series of haunting characters born from her subconscious, forcing her to untangle the emotional truths behind each tale.

faq.answer: I Am Frankelda is primarily a gothic musical dark fantasy and animated horror-fantasy film, blending spooky elements with musical numbers and emotional drama.
faq.question: What is the dominant genre of I Am Frankelda?

faq.answer: Yes, I Am Frankelda is part of a larger universe; it serves as a feature-length prequel to the animated series Frankelda's Book of Spooks (Sustos ocultos de Frankelda).
faq.question: Is this movie part of a franchise?

faq.answer: The film was crafted using stop-motion animation, making history as the first feature film from Mexico made entirely with stop-motion puppets and sets.
faq.question: What animation technique was used to make I Am Frankelda?

faq.answer: The movie was written, directed, and produced by the Mexican filmmaking brothers Roy Ambriz and Arturo Ambriz (the Ambriz Bros).
faq.question: Who directed I Am Frankelda?

faq.answer: No, there is no extra scene hidden after the credits end, though the credit sequence itself features additional artwork and original music from the film.
faq.question: Is there a post-credit scene in I Am Frankelda?

faq.answer: The story takes place in 19th-century post-colonial Mexico and expands into the surreal fantasy world of Topus Terrentus within the protagonist's subconscious mind.
faq.question: What is the setting of I Am Frankelda?

faq.answer: The film follows Francisca Imelda, a gifted young writer in 19th-century Mexico whose spooky stories are dismissed by society. She is thrust into her subconscious realm, where she meets a trapped prince and must face her own dark creations to balance fiction and reality.
faq.question: What is the plot of I Am Frankelda?

faq.answer: The film was originally produced in Spanish, and English audio dubbing and subbed versions were made available for international distribution.
faq.question: What is the original language of the film?

faq.answer: While it features spooky themes, monsters, and dark fantasy elements similar to films like Coraline or The Nightmare Before Christmas, it is generally intended for older children, pre-teens, and family audiences who enjoy gothic fantasy.
faq.question: Is I Am Frankelda suitable for children?

faq.answer: The film was created and produced by the Mexico City-based animation studio Cinema Fantasma, in association with Warner Bros. Discovery Kids & Animation.
faq.question: Which studio produced I Am Frankelda?
